newsitem.title: USA: Raines sees modest impact from any U.S. rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Raines sees modest impact from any U.S. rate rise.

text.p: The head of the White House Office of Management and Budget on Tuesday said that any increase in short-term U.S. interest rates would have only a modest impact on the economy.
"It would depend a lot on how the real economy responded to that," White House budget chief Franklin Raines told a conference of America's Community Bankers.
"If you just isolate simply an increase in short-term interest rates, it would have a modest negative effect," he said.
"If the tightening of short-term rates were to bring down longer term rates and it didn't have any other macroeconomic effect then it would have a neutral to a positive effect," Raines added.
